flags.correction: Cl. 10.10: one free question per registration, due three days after registration closes (1 Nov unless the portal says otherwise), and only the five most-voted reach the jury. An answer is not assured; N0 is the standing default.
flags.detail: S47 (fetch-tool summary; browser check needed). Registration closes 29 Oct, so asking needs registration first. The page shows 3 Nov; the tool shows both dates.

flags.claim: Contacting the one Coast Salish juror and her firm is the juror-contact risk (M01 contact_guard).
flags.correction: Cl. 5.2 bars approaching any of seven jurors or the undefined Commissioning Party; cl. 8.3 voids prizes. The jury includes UBC SALA's Matthew Soules. The guard covers all seven jurors and firms, the Commissioning Party and Buildner's advisors.
flags.detail: S34, S47. SALA desk crits from him are a risk for UBC entrants. The City page names the City as host; the FAQ names Buildner with the City and SALA.

flags.claim: M07 ai_involvement maps 'composite' to compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia and 'assistive edit' to algorithmicallyEnhanced.
flags.correction: IPTC defines compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia as 'Edited using Generative AI' (inpainting, outpainting) and compositeSynthetic as a mix with at least one generative element. algorithmicallyEnhanced is non-generative only. Enum split into generative and non-generative edits; mapping rewritten.
flags.detail: S38 re-read 21 Oct 2026. The old mapping would have labelled generative fill as mere enhancement, understating AI use. Mapping now shown with each term's definition and URI; vocabulary re-read at each release.

flags.claim: Per-view height rules for the 24 cones sit in the Public Views Guidelines (2024), and the 24-record dataset is a fixed match to the July 2024 set (M06).
flags.correction: The dataset says the authoritative source for the views is the City's bylaws and that the extract is updated as needed; it was modified 19 Oct 2026. M06 links touched cones to the governing by-law or plan as well as the Guidelines, and re-checks count and ids at each export.
flags.detail: S32 API metadata read 21 Oct 2026: 24 records, ids stored in M06. The specific by-law was not identified: no opened source names it (S57, S58 name none; City pages 403). A person must find it.

flags.claim: FPIC is obtained only by States, so it is not claimable by an entrant (M02 claimable_by_entrant basis).
flags.correction: TRC Call 92(i) asks the corporate sector to seek FPIC before economic development projects. FPIC stays locked for entrants because a hypothetical competition entry has no real project and, at N0-N3, no engagement.
flags.detail: S04 Call 92(i), text extracted from the PDF in r3; S01 Arts. 19 and 32(2) address States. The lock is unchanged; only the basis is corrected.

flags.claim: S48 is an undated CIRNAC page whose title was not captured.
flags.correction: The page is 'Updated Guidelines for Federal Officials to Fulfill the Duty to Consult', March 2011: guidance for federal officials that may be dated. It says third parties such as proponents have no legal obligation to consult.
flags.detail: S48 Part B, s.I, read in r3. The third-party line supports the ban on duty-sense 'consulted' wording; the Crown keeps the duty and may delegate only procedural tasks.

flags.claim: A BC legislative session is under way in fall 2026 and may act on DRIPA (r3 critique, M02 badge note).
flags.correction: The Assembly adjourned 28 May 2026 and the 43rd Parliament was dissolved 22 Sep 2026; a general election is on 24 Oct 2026. No sitting can act before the election. BC Laws shows the Act current to 13 Oct 2026.
flags.detail: S70 (leg.bc.ca), S71 (elections.bc.ca), S02. The Premier's working group and the repeal petition (due 25 Jan 2027, S60) continue; the new government's DRIPA position is unknown.

flags.claim: The Musqueam page lists eight package items and applicability to ideas competitions is ambiguous only because of item 2 (S10, M01).
flags.correction: The page lists eight named items plus an open-ended additional-documents line, and asks for contact at initial planning of all projects within Musqueam territory. That sentence is the real source of the ambiguity. N0 stays default.
flags.detail: S10 re-read r3. No fees, student or academic mention. Whether a hypothetical entry is a project within the territory is the Nation's to say; the tool does not decide.

flags.claim: Sen̓áḵw facts in M04 (58 storeys; services list; no City approvals needed) are plain precedent facts without speaker or conflict.
flags.correction: S54: the services list is Mayor Kennedy Stewart's statement; 'no City approvals needed' is the reporter's own. S16 gives 58 storeys and also 56 for 'some buildings'; Dezeen gives 12-58. Each fact carries a speaker tag and a conflict chip.
flags.detail: S54, S16, S17 re-read r3. 58 is the later, more specific figure; the 56 claim cites a 2020 source and is not reconciled. Both shown.

flags.claim: ExifTool can strip author and GPS fields from competition PDFs (M07 library role, cut #1 and the identity-field metric).
flags.correction: ExifTool edits PDFs by reversible incremental update and never deletes old data, so original Author, Creator and XMP values stay recoverable. Pipeline now: delete /Info and XMP (pikepdf), strip image and object metadata, full qpdf rewrite, raw-byte scan, fixture test with a recovery attempt. ExifTool is for non-PDF images and read-only scans.
flags.detail: S72 and S73 opened r4: 'all metadata edits are reversible'; ExifTool alone may not be used to securely edit PDF metadata; recover with -PDF-update:all=; qpdf rewrite removes old data. A scan of current tags alone would report 0 while names stay in the file. Also missed before: image EXIF and XMP, XMP history paths, _original backups.

flags.claim: The new BC government's DRIPA position is unknown (M02 badge_states, r3 flag on the legislative session).
flags.correction: Parties' stated positions are known: S60 (critic-read r4) reports the Conservative Party said it would repeal DRIPA and a Conservative MLA applied for a repeal petition. Only the 24 Oct election result is open. Badge reads: election 24 Oct; parties' positions differ; outcome pending; re-check 25 to 27 Oct.
flags.detail: S60 not re-opened by this agent in r4 (fetch limit). Elections BC (S71) is the source for the result. The 14-day chip and the 25 Nov re-check would have missed the result, so an event-based re-check is added.

flags.claim: Every image with no AI maps to digitalCreation, with humanEdits for edited captures (M07 mapping, r3).
flags.correction: IPTC defines digitalCreation as media created by a human with non-generative tools, so it does not fit a camera capture. Unedited photo: digitalCapture. Edited capture: humanEdits. Montage of renders and captures with no AI: composite. Montage where every element is a capture: compositeCapture.
flags.detail: S38 re-read r4. 'Composite' is defined as any element may or may not be generative, so it does not understate AI use; the visible label states the declared level. Rule kept: when unsure, use the term that discloses more AI use.

flags.claim: Canadian Indigenous design charters published by Nations or Indigenous design bodies exist for tall-building design.
flags.correction: None found for tall buildings or Coast Salish territory. The closest instrument is the International Indigenous Design Charter (S49), which is Australian-led.
flags.detail: No Nation-published design guideline for downtown towers was found in r1 or r2.

flags.claim: City of Vancouver policy documents (UNDRIP Strategy PDF, Action Plan 2024-2028, Higher Buildings Policy PDF and review PDF, Heather Lands statement, per-view pages, Public Views Guidelines) say what the packet summarises.
flags.detail: vancouver.ca, bylaws, guidelines and syc domains returned 403 again in r3; shapeyourcity.ca opened (S66, S67). The 32-of-79 figure and the Heather date come from search summaries. A teammate must open these in a browser.

flags.claim: The Higher Buildings Policy was amended in July 2018 and renamed from 'General Policy for Higher Buildings' (critic, via search summary).
flags.detail: Not seen in S66 or S67, which say established 1997, reviewed 2011, minor upper-limit changes since. H005 returned 403. M02 shows the amendment as unverified until a person opens the PDF.

flags.claim: City view cones carry height limits the tool can read, and the by-law that sets them is known.
flags.detail: Dataset description says development in the polygons is height-limited; no height field; the authoritative source is the City's bylaws (S32). Which by-law or plan, and the permitted heights, are unknown. Plan intersection is only a trigger to check.

flags.claim: OCAP can be named, badged or implemented as a compliance label in the tool.
flags.detail: Secondary sources say OCAP is an FNIGC registered trademark; FNIGC pages returned 403. Do not display OCAP-compliant; cite OCAP only as principles with a link.

flags.claim: Sen̓áḵw developer statements (consultation process, net-zero claim, below-market rents) are established facts.
flags.detail: They are the project's or developer's statements (senakw.com, Dezeen; Nch'ḵay̓ representative). Show them as stated, with an as-of date. S16 gives two settlement dates (2001, June 2000) and two height figures.

flags.claim: BC Sans or another open font covers every codepoint in the Nation-name registry.
flags.detail: BC Sans README says modified Noto Sans with BC Indigenous-language support; no characters named, licence unread. Gentium is OFL-1.1; First Nations orthographies unconfirmed. M05 and M07 test coverage per string.

flags.claim: The signing certificate in a C2PA manifest identifies the team or an individual, or a signer organisation (CAI docs per critic).
flags.detail: C2PA 2.3 requires the certificate chain (s14.5) and a claim_generator_info name; subject-field rules were not found in the text read. Rule: credentials off in competition mode; if on, neutral organisation and generic text.

flags.claim: In April 2026 the BC government proposed suspending key DRIPA sections (critic).
flags.detail: Not found. S60 reports the Premier reversed a plan to amend DRIPA in April 2026 and set a working group; S59 reports SCC leave. BC Laws shows no change to 13 Oct 2026 (S02). Post-election position unknown.

flags.claim: Canadian copyright treatment of AI-assisted images is settled enough for the tool to state ownership.
flags.detail: It is not. The SURYAST registration is challenged in CIPPIC v. Sahni (T-1717-24, filed July 2024; no ruling found, S62). The ISED consultation (S63) is unopened. The tool never states copyright status.

flags.claim: Generative upscaling counts as a generative edit (compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia) under IPTC.
flags.detail: IPTC's wording covers augmentation, correction or enhancement using a generative model (S38), which includes generative upscaling; no IPTC example names upscaling. Team reading; when unsure, use the term that discloses more AI use.

flags.claim: The Buildner jury page, Terms clause numbers, Q&A dates and juror strings are as the fetch summaries said.
flags.detail: Never read by a person in a browser in five rounds. r3: WebFetch timed out and the browser returned 502/504. r4: WebFetch timed out twice; critic got HTTP 502. M01's full guard card is blocked until a person records verified-by and date.

flags.claim: SCC item 21510 (linked from S59) is the docket for the Gitxaała appeal.
flags.correction: Critic r4: SCC docket 21510 is an unrelated 1989 Manitoba case (S79, not opened by this agent). Docket and BCCA neutral citation fields stay empty until a person records them from scc-csc.ca or bccourts.ca.
flags.detail: S59 gives no docket or hearing date. S68 is not opened. A wrong docket in a badge would send users to the wrong case.

flags.claim: InDesign and Illustrator PDFs carry private application data (for example PieceInfo or embedded editing data) holding author or file-path metadata that the strip must remove.
flags.detail: Team reading from general PDF practice; no source opened. The scan treats unknown private-data entries as hits for a human until the tool is run on real exports from InDesign, Illustrator and Rhino.

flags.claim: Embedded JPEG streams keep EXIF, XMP and GPS when a PDF is exported from InDesign, Illustrator, Rhino or a browser.
flags.detail: Untested. The strip treats every image stream as a leak path and the fixture PDF includes a geotagged JPEG. A person must test each export route the teams use.

flags.claim: Zero-tolerance gates (no wording above declared status, no unresolved cultural-content flags, no missing AI labels, no identity-bearing fields on export).
flags.detail: Platform rules chosen by the team, backed by principles in S01, S04, S22, S28, S47, not by published numeric thresholds. Editable and shown in the team-assumption colour.

flags.claim: The engagement ladder (N0-N4 per Nation), the claim-vocabulary list and the ai_involvement-to-IPTC mapping.
flags.detail: Team designs, not published standards. Rung names, phrase lists and channel locks need paid Indigenous review before release. The stage A ban list is an unreviewed platform rule. The IPTC mapping uses IPTC's own definitions but the choice of term per level is the team's.

flags.claim: The as-is workflow of entrants is reconstructed from the brief and typical practice.
flags.detail: Not observed. Test with two or three student teams, after the ethics check (see UNRESOLVED flag), before relying on pain points.

flags.claim: Effort estimates (about 47 person-days across P07) and the staged scope.
flags.detail: Unvalidated guesses. r4 core subset: M01 stage A 3.5 + M06 georeference and cones 2 + M07 10.5 = 16 person-days (r3: 14); ray casting stays v1. Core checkpoint 13 Nov is 23 days away; submission 30 Nov is 40 days; two students on other packets.

flags.claim: For VTC 2026 the entrant product is the offline strip tool, M01 stage A, M06 geometry and M07; CULT cards, lists and Nation strings ship only after Indigenous review, likely after 30 Nov.
flags.detail: No reviewer, budget or contact exists; registration closes in 8 days. Modules still name the 30% criterion as a target, but the entrant product does not cover it fully. Stated honestly in M08.

flags.claim: M07 core cut order, target dates and the private-mode test protocol.
flags.detail: Cut order: offline strip, scan and fixture test; AI label plus IPTC term; source-id lint; glyph check; PROV fields. Target dates 13 Nov, 20 Nov, then not before 30 Nov. Private-mode test checks are the team's design, owned with the platform packet.

flags.claim: The nine private-mode test cases, the 14-day validity of a test record, the Buildner decision date of 27 Oct, and the strip scan rules (startxref count, /Prev, deny-list, decompressed copy).
flags.detail: Team designs, no published standard; S76 supports the rule that noindex, not robots.txt, keeps a URL out of search. The strip pipeline is documented from S72 to S75 but was not run in r4: no tools installed and installing needs a download approval. The xref-count test is the team's reading of PDF structure; confirm on the fixture.

flags.claim: Whether entrants should contact the three Nations about a hypothetical competition entry, and through which channel.
flags.detail: No statement on the Buildner page, Terms or any Nation page opened. Musqueam asks for contact at initial planning of all projects within its territory (S10); whether that reaches an ideas entry is unstated. N0 (no contact) stays default. Draft the portal question now; it may not reach the jury.

flags.claim: Squamish Nation and Tsleil-Waututh Nation published referral or engagement requirements comparable to Musqueam's.
flags.detail: Not found in r1 to r3. Squamish home page lists no referral page. TWN guides (S52) unread; TWN protocol page (S53) describes no outside-request process.

flags.claim: Indigenous reviewer sign-off: who, who pays, whether before 30 Nov 2026.
flags.detail: Required: a paid reviewer independent of Nation referral offices, jurors and Buildner advisors. No person or budget identified. Team assumption: name a budget line and contact the reviewer by 28 Oct; fallback is no CULT content for VTC 2026.

flags.claim: Spelling of Squamish and Halkomelem strings in the registry (example: Hiy̓ám̓ Housing; the 2018 plaza names).
flags.detail: The fetch tool garbles combining marks and sources disagree. Every string must be copied by a person from the Nation's page, stored in NFC and compared by codepoint.

flags.claim: Real-world location of the hypothetical VTC block.
flags.detail: Buildner page gives only the downtown core and a downloadable 3D model; no coordinates. M06 requires the team to enter a georeference and say whether it comes from the brief or is a team assumption. Brief-derived values stay local (see Terms IP flag).

flags.claim: VTC brief values: criterion weights, cultural-context wording, anonymity clause, site coordinates (S35 unopened after four rounds).
flags.detail: A release precondition: M07 export mode and M08 do not ship until a registered team member opens the brief and records version, date and the anonymity clause. Registration closes 29 Oct. Until then every brief-derived value shows 'from supplied summary'. If Buildner stays down, the M08 fallback scope applies.

flags.claim: Who 'Commissioning Party' is in Terms cl. 5.2 and 10.5, and whether registered entrants may use the City's higherbuilding inbox.
flags.detail: Undefined in the Terms. The City page names the City as host (S66), making it the likeliest candidate (team reading); the FAQ names Buildner with the City and SALA (S67). The guard now names City staff and inboxes and warns that material sent there may be published; ask Buildner to define the term.

flags.claim: Whether user tests with student teams and the Indigenous review need research-ethics approval at UBC.
flags.detail: TCPS 2 Art. 2.1 covers course-based activities with participants (S64); UBC says instructors usually apply once (S65); Ch. 9 applies if Indigenous people take part; UBC has an Indigenous review page (S69). Ask the instructor and BREB; do not self-classify.

flags.claim: Whether the platform packet will deliver tested private, no-fork, no-index competition projects, and a local or offline build, by 13 Nov.
flags.detail: M07 depends on them and has no control over them. The offline strip tool does not. Until a dated record of all nine test cases exists in M08, the VTC flag is not offered on the hosted platform and entrants are told to work locally or offline.

flags.claim: What entrants do if Buildner stays unreachable or registration fails before 29 Oct, so the brief and Terms are never read.
flags.detail: Decision date 27 Oct (team assumption): a person checks Buildner status through its general support channel, never a juror or advisor, and logs each attempt. M08 holds a pre-written fallback scope: M07 export mode and the full contact guard do not ship; entrants get M01 stage A (generic rule), M06 geometry and the offline strip tool on generic rules.

flags.claim: Whether UBC SALA students or course projects are 'associates' of the Organizer or Jury under cl. 3.3.5, and whether SALA is part of the Organizer.
flags.detail: The authors are UBC M.Arch students; the FAQ credits SALA (S67); juror Soules is SALA faculty (S34). M01 now requires each author's declaration, a question to Buildner staff (never a juror, asked without describing the entry) and the instructor's written confirmation that no juror reviews VTC-specific work in the course.

flags.claim: Whether the Terms' IP and confidentiality clauses allow brief-derived data (coordinates, site-plan labels, text, the 3D model) in a public, forkable repository.
flags.detail: Terms unread (S47 is a fetch summary of other clauses). Until a person reads them and records the clause reference in M08, brief-derived values stay in each entrant's local or private project and the platform ships an empty georeference field.

modules.name: Per-Nation engagement ledger, claims lint, contact guard and eligibility check
modules.design_question: What can this entry truthfully say about engagement with each Nation, whom must entrants not contact, and is the team eligible?
modules.effort: Stage A 3.5 person-days (N0 statement, contact guard, eligibility and affiliation check, ban-list lint; unreviewed beta); stage B 3 more after Indigenous review. Source verification is a person task and gates the full guard card.
depends_on: review_state manifest flag (set in M08 register; no runtime dependency)
Person-made dated PDF snapshot of the Buildner jury page and Terms (verified-by, date), or the M08 fallback scope
PRES board text nodes (other packet; optional, pasted text also works)
inputs: Project metadata: site, competition entry flag
Per-Nation declared status, counterpart type, evidence note
Organizer Q&A log (question, date, pasted answer)
Board and narrative text from PRES nodes or pasted
Eligibility answers per author (private)
Buildner staff reply on associates and instructor written confirmation (private records)
Source snapshot record (verified-by, date, PDF reference)
Nation-name registry from M05 (stage B)
outputs: engagement_ledger.json (per Nation: status, counterpart, date, declared-by, evidence, authorization reference)
claims_lint_report (phrase, location, Nation, minimum status, pass/fail)
contact_guard_card (seven jurors with firms, City staff, Commissioning Party, advisors, verified-by and date, acknowledged flag)

parameters.name: engagement_status_per_nation
parameters.unit: enum per Nation (Musqueam, Squamish, Tsleil-Waututh): N0 no contact (default); N1 desk research only (not engagement); N2 organizer Q&A answer logged (not engagement); N3 conversation with a person, counterpart recorded; N4 written permission from an authorized decision-maker for one stated use
parameters.relationship: Higher status permits stronger wording for that Nation only. N1 allows wording that names the documents read, never engagement wording. One Nation's status says nothing about the other two.

parameters.name: counterpart_type
parameters.unit: enum: community member, Indigenous artist or consultant, Nation staff, authorized Nation representative, Nation-owned corporation
parameters.relationship: Only a written decision from an authorized representative supports approved-by wording; other types support only spoke-with wording. Team design; the Indigenous reviewer sets the final list.

parameters.name: claim_vocabulary
parameters.unit: phrase list mapped to minimum status and counterpart
parameters.relationship: Duty-sense 'consulted' is banned: the duty sits with the Crown, and federal guidance says third parties have no legal obligation to consult. Approved-by needs an authorized-decision reference. Collaboration phrases on the ban list are barred for N0-N3.

parameters.name: stage_a_freeze_rule
parameters.unit: frozen ban-list and N0-text version with hash; any addition goes through review_state
parameters.relationship: Stage A ships only claim-restricting rules and fixed text with no cultural content. Freezing the list and the N0 text stops a later edit adding cultural wording that would skip the review gate in M08.

parameters.name: juror_and_firm_list
parameters.unit: De Vries (MVRDV); Gill (AS+GG); Baker (K̓ESU+CO); Cheng (James K.M. Cheng Architects); MacDougall (Focal Engineering); Lee (PWL Partnership); Soules (Matthew Soules Architecture, UBC SALA)
parameters.relationship: Naming every juror and firm lets entrants avoid contact by name, including no feedback on the entry from Soules or in SALA reviews he attends. Strings are copied by a person from a dated snapshot and rechecked at each release.

parameters.name: contact_guard
parameters.unit: fixed card, verified-by and date, acknowledgement flag; required before any export
parameters.relationship: Cl. 5.2 bars approaching any juror or the Commissioning Party; cl. 8.3 voids prizes. Advisors (cl. 10.4) are unnamed; entrants must not seek them out. Questions go through the portal only.

parameters.name: city_staff_no_contact_list
parameters.unit: Cory Dobson (Senior Planner, Community Planning; higherbuildings@vancouver.ca); Josh White (General Manager, Planning, Urban Design and Sustainability); views@vancouver.ca (view-cone dataset contact)
parameters.relationship: The City hosts the competition and may be the Commissioning Party, so entrants avoid contact about the entry. The City page invites ideas by email; the critic read that these may be featured on the City website, a publication risk under cl. 4.1 (S66 not re-opened r4). Not a channel for entries.

parameters.name: guard_source_verification
parameters.unit: verified-by, date, dated PDF snapshot per quoted clause number, date and juror string
parameters.relationship: A wrong name, clause or date would steer entrants into contact or a missed deadline. Until a person confirms, the card shows only the generic no-contact rule, with no names, dates or clause numbers. If Buildner stays down, the M08 fallback scope applies.

parameters.name: commissioning_party_rule
parameters.unit: text rule plus a question for Buildner
parameters.relationship: The Terms never define Commissioning Party. The City page names the City as host, so the City is the likeliest candidate (team reading); the FAQ names Buildner with the City and SALA. Entrants use published City documents only.

parameters.name: eligibility_self_check
parameters.unit: yes/no card quoting cl. 3.3.5; private record per author, including whether the author will enter VTC
parameters.relationship: Cl. 3.3.5 bars employees, interns, contractors and associates or family of the Organizer or Jury; 'associate' is undefined. Uncertain cases go to Buildner staff, never a juror. Each author records their own status in the README.

parameters.name: associate_question_and_instructor_confirmation
parameters.unit: two records: Buildner staff reply (question, date, answer) and the instructor's written confirmation
parameters.relationship: The FAQ credits UBC SALA and a juror is SALA faculty, so SALA students or course projects may count as associates. Ask Buildner staff after a person has read cl. 5 and 10, without describing the entry. Instructor confirms in writing that no juror reviews VTC-specific work in the course.

parameters.name: non_endorsement_disclaimer
parameters.unit: fixed text agreed with the instructor: student-built open-source tool, not an official tool of and not endorsed by the City of Vancouver, Buildner or UBC SALA; no logos or wordmarks of those bodies
parameters.relationship: A public tool built for a named competition inside a partner school can look official and imply Organizer endorsement. The text shows on every platform page, README, export checklist and tool report; not on boards, which stay anonymous.

parameters.name: qa_route
parameters.unit: dates and counts shown on the card
parameters.relationship: Cl. 10.10: one free question per registration, due three days after the 29 Oct close (1 Nov unless the portal says otherwise; page says 3 Nov); only the top five voted reach the jury. N0 stays the standing default.

parameters.name: referral_reference_items
parameters.unit: count 0-8 named items plus an open-ended additional-documents line; reference only, real-project mode
parameters.relationship: Musqueam's list describes a real project with regulatory permits and asks for contact at initial planning of all projects in its territory. Applicability to ideas competitions is unestablished, so the entrant flow never prompts a referral.

parameters.name: nation_name_strings
parameters.unit: NFC strings with source URL, retrieval date, codepoints (stage B)
parameters.relationship: Names copied from each Nation's own page keep the Nation in charge of how it is named; typed or machine-translated strings misrepresent people and places. Equivalent sequences must match after normalization.

metrics.name: Wording above declared status, per Nation
metrics.basis: Platform rule: consent and consultation are decided by Nations and governments, so claims of them must be true. Lint checks wording only.
metrics.method: Phrase lint of board text against each Nation's declared status.

metrics.name: Banned or unsupported phrases (duty-sense consulted; unreferenced approved or endorsed; collaboration phrases at N0-N3)
metrics.basis: The duty to consult cannot be delegated and third parties have no legal obligation to consult (S48, 2011 guidance); UNDRIP Arts. 19 and 32(2) address States. Zero is a platform rule; list unreviewed and frozen.
metrics.method: Fixed ban list in stage A; extended list after review.

metrics.name: Per-Nation status and evidence note declared at export
metrics.good: yes for all three, with evidence note for N2-N4
metrics.basis: Course rule: every result shows its work.
metrics.method: Check ledger exists and is complete.

metrics.name: Contact guard acknowledged (all seven jurors and firms, City staff, Commissioning Party, advisors)
metrics.good: yes, before any export
metrics.bad: no, or guard lists fewer than seven jurors
metrics.basis: r1 guard named one juror. Cl. 5.2 and 8.3 cover all jurors and the Commissioning Party, including UBC SALA's Soules; r3 adds named City staff; r4 adds the City-inbox publication warning. Acknowledgement is a platform rule.
metrics.method: Check the guard text and the flag before export.

metrics.name: Guard source verification (verified-by and date) recorded before the full card is shown
metrics.good: yes; otherwise only the generic rule shows
metrics.bad: full card with names, dates and clauses shown unverified
metrics.basis: Terms, jury page and dates were read only through fetch summaries; Buildner was unreachable in r3 and r4. Platform rule.
metrics.method: Check the record exists and carries a date.

metrics.name: Eligibility and affiliation records before export: each author's declaration, Buildner associate question logged, instructor confirmation
metrics.good: yes for all three records
metrics.basis: Cl. 3.3.5 excludes associates of the Organizer or Jury; SALA's role is unclear (S67, S34); ineligibility could void an entry. Platform rule to prompt the checks.
metrics.method: Check the private records exist and carry dates.

metrics.name: Non-endorsement text on every platform page, README, export checklist and tool report
metrics.good: yes
metrics.bad: missing on any, or logo of City, Buildner or UBC shown
metrics.basis: A tool built in a partner school for a named competition can look official. Kept off boards to protect anonymity. Wording needs the instructor's agreement.
metrics.method: Scan page templates and report templates.

metrics.name: Nation-channel question: both dates shown and N0 stated as standing default
metrics.good: yes
metrics.bad: 3 Nov shown alone, or a sanctioned channel implied
metrics.basis: r1 treated the Q&A as able to settle the question by 3 Nov. Cl. 10.10 sets 1 Nov by default, one free question, top-five vote.
metrics.method: Check card text.

metrics.name: Referral-pack completeness (Musqueam list)
metrics.unit: items present of 8 named, reference only
metrics.good: Not applicable to competition entries; real projects only
metrics.bad: Entrant flow prompts, counts or scores completeness
metrics.basis: Round 0 marked 8 of 8 verified. The page verifies a list (eight items plus additional documents), not that it applies to an ideas competition.
metrics.method: Checklist rendered only in real-project mode.

metrics.name: Indigenous-language strings with Nation source and NFC form (stage B)

modules.method: A YAML deck. Ten starter cards are indexed to the charter's ten protocols, each paraphrased in one line and linked, because the book bars reproduction; four team cards cover benefit, place names, what the team will not do, and a static do-not-derive-form-from card. Each card has a prompt, a source badge, a what-the-tool-can-check line and a what-only-people-or-Nations-can-answer line. Users choose one of four states: not considered, considering, responded with evidence, needs Nation input. The channel selector locks form, naming, pattern and commissioned art unless the status for that Nation is N4 for that use. Provenance cards call M05; land, water and view cards call M06. The deck is gated by review_state and is not part of the VTC 2026 entrant product. No numeric aggregation.

Channel selector with padlock icons on locked channels and the reason shown
No radar chart, no totals; per-column counts as a plain list
modules.human_judgment: All of it: which principles apply, how to read them, what to change in the design, and when to stop and ask the Nations. The tool only prompts and records.
modules.limits: No Nation-published guideline for tall buildings was found. The charter is Australian-led and self-regulated; no Coast Salish contributor is named; territorial law prevails. Cards are prompts, not approvals, and say so. Unreviewed until sign-off.

Reference-image uploads

modules.method: 1) Every asset, including reference images, enters a manifest with hash, source URL, licence, author, AI-use field and declared authorship. 2) A human sets the cultural-content flag; keyword assist only suggests. 3) A flagged asset needs a permission record before the gate turns green. 4) AI prompts and reference images are checked against an editable, advisor-curated term list; Indigenous motif, pattern or sacred-image generation is refused with a clause link and logged. 5) Board text is scanned for borrowed-form phrases; hits are amber for review. 6) Nation-held layers are stored as URL plus retrieval date, never cached. 7) Registry strings are stored in NFC and glyph-checked. 8) Notices and Labels from a Hub project ID show read-only once Hub terms are read. modules.name: City in Nature and skyline identity prompts with georeferenced view geometry

inputs: Layer 0 tower geometry, heights, public-space tags
Site boundary, labelled directions on the VTC site plan (rotated north arrow; from supplied summary until brief opened) and the user's georeference, entered in a local or private project only
Context massing: existing and approved towers (SITE)
City view-cone polygons (open data) with dataset modified and retrieval dates
User-placed viewpoints tagged public or private amenity
Declared materials with origin, planting palette, water features

cone_intersections.json (ids, links, rule-to-check flag, by-law and guideline fields, dataset snapshot, 'information only' label)

parameters.name: brief_data_handling
parameters.unit: rule: brief-derived values (coordinates, site-plan labels, text, 3D model) held only in the entrant's local or private project; the public platform and repository ship an empty georeference field
parameters.relationship: Brief materials go to registrants and may carry Buildner copyright or use limits; the Terms' IP and confidentiality clauses are unread. Committing them to a public, forkable repository could breach the Terms and hand brief content to non-registrants.

parameters.name: site_georeference
parameters.unit: lat/lon of a block corner, grid rotation in degrees, source (brief or team assumption)
parameters.relationship: The block is hypothetical but cone polygons and bearings are real. Placement decides which cones the massing touches and which bearings apply, so cone and azimuth outputs stay blocked until it is set and printed on every output.

parameters.name: viewpoint_set
parameters.unit: points (x, y, eye height) tagged public or private amenity
parameters.relationship: Public-realm points carry the City in Nature and view-protection argument; terraces and typical floors are private amenity views, reported separately. Higher points see more azimuth; ground points depend on podium height and tower spacing.

parameters.name: target_bearing_ranges
parameters.unit: degrees from site-plan labels
parameters.relationship: The brief's north arrow is rotated against the street grid, so bearings come from the labelled directions (Stanley Park, BC Place, Entertainment District, Burrard Inlet, North Shore Mountains); assuming true north reports views toward the wrong landmark.

parameters.name: obstruction_context
parameters.unit: set of existing and approved towers
parameters.relationship: More approved towers in the same height range narrow the unobstructed azimuth at public-realm viewpoints, so tower spacing and orientation change the views public space keeps.

parameters.name: tower_face_width_toward_viewpoint
parameters.unit: m and degrees subtended
parameters.relationship: A wider face toward the Queen Elizabeth Park bearing subtends a larger angle in the skyline view; a slimmer face or rotation subtends less. Geometry, not a cultural claim.

parameters.name: view_cone_intersection
parameters.unit: which of the 24 dataset cones the massing intersects in plan; output labelled information only
parameters.relationship: Development inside a polygon is height-limited, so an intersection means the governing rule for that view must be checked: the applicable by-law or plan (a person identifies it) and the Public Views Guidelines (2024). No heights in the data; zero intersections is not clearance; entrants likely cannot get authoritative heights before 30 Nov.

parameters.name: dataset_snapshot_and_recheck
parameters.unit: modified date, retrieval date, total_count, id list. 21 Oct 2026: modified 19 Oct; 24 ids: J1, J2, 3.2.1, 3.2.2, 3.2.3, 3.2.4, 9.1, 9.2, 10, 20, 21, 22, 27.1, 27.2, 28, A, B1, B2, D, E, G1, G2, H, K
parameters.relationship: The dataset is updated as needed, so a stale cone set changes which cones the massing touches. Each export re-queries count and ids and warns if count is not 24 or ids differ from the stored set.

parameters.name: place_and_feature_names
parameters.unit: City name from City data; Nation name only after review_state release; each with source; never translated
parameters.relationship: Until Indigenous sign-off M06 shows City names and geometry only. After release, Nation and City names appear side by side, keeping naming authority with their sources; no cultural meaning is derived from a direction.

parameters.name: cultural_prompt_cards
parameters.unit: skyline-identity and Nation-view cards, gated by review_state
parameters.relationship: Cards that mention Nations, Indigenous meaning or cultural identity are cultural content: hidden from entrants until reviewed, so unreviewed prompts do not shape entries. City in Nature and material-origin prompts stay open.

parameters.name: material_origin_and_nature_declaration
parameters.unit: free text with source
parameters.relationship: A declared origin and an evidence link turn local material and City in Nature from adjectives into checkable statements; no sourced numeric threshold was found. A cultural claim about a material is locked by M03 below N4.

metrics.name: Unobstructed azimuth toward target bearings, baseline versus proposal, public viewpoints first (v1)
metrics.good: No net loss versus the context-only baseline, or loss documented with a mitigation note
metrics.basis: No sourced threshold exists; editable team preset that asks for explanation rather than scoring.
metrics.method: Ray cast at 1-degree steps over context-only and context-plus-proposal models, public and private separate.

metrics.name: View cones whose polygons the massing intersects in plan
metrics.good: Each touched or nearby cone listed with its governing by-law or plan and guideline rule, checked by a person in a browser; output labelled information only
metrics.bad: Zero intersections reported as clearance, or a touched cone with no checked rule
metrics.basis: r1 wrongly called the set partial. Council kept 24 views on 10 Jul 2024; the dataset matched on 21 Oct 2026 but says by-laws are authoritative and is updated as needed. No heights; zero is not clearance.
metrics.method: Polygon intersection in plan using the georeference; each result marked rule to be checked; dataset caveat shown on the table.

metrics.name: Dataset snapshot re-checked at export: count 24, ids equal to stored set, dates printed
metrics.good: yes; any difference warned
metrics.bad: count or ids differ with no warning, or dates not printed
metrics.basis: r2 treated the 24-record match as fixed; the dataset was modified 19 Oct 2026 and is updated as needed.
metrics.method: Re-query total_count and ids at each export; compare with the stored list.

metrics.name: Brief-derived values stored in public platform data, fixtures or the public repository
metrics.basis: The Terms' IP and confidentiality clauses are unread; brief materials are registrant-only. Platform rule until a person records the clause reference in M08.
metrics.method: Scan repository, fixtures and knowledge-base files for brief-sourced coordinates, labels, text and model files.

metrics.name: Queen Elizabeth Park silhouette reported (v1)
metrics.unit: angular width and height in degrees, from user-entered viewpoint
metrics.good: Reported for the viewpoint and compared with park cones 3.2.1-3.2.4
metrics.bad: Not produced, or produced from a guessed viewpoint
metrics.basis: The brief recommends a skyline view from the park (supplied summary); cones 3.2.1-3.2.4 were retained in 2024; viewpoint coordinates are not hard-coded.
metrics.method: Perspective projection of baseline and proposal.

metrics.name: Georeference set and printed on outputs
metrics.good: yes, with source (brief or team assumption)
metrics.bad: no, or not shown on an output
metrics.basis: Round 0 critic: the block is hypothetical, so every view output depends on placement. The Buildner page gives no coordinates.
metrics.method: Check stamp on each output.

metrics.name: Cultural prompt cards or Nation-language strings visible to entrants without review sign-off
metrics.basis: Release gate is keyed to content, not category. M06 is ECOL but shows names and cards.
metrics.method: Check card and string manifests for review_state.

metrics.name: Prompt cards answered with an evidence link
metrics.good: all cards carry an answer and evidence link or needs input
metrics.basis: Course rule; no scoring of nature or culture.
metrics.method: Count states.

modules.method: 1) The user sets the georeference (block corner, grid rotation, source) in a local or private project; until then cone and azimuth outputs stay blocked and the public platform ships the field empty. 2) Import massing and context from Layer 0 and SITE. 3) Intersect the massing outline with the 24 dataset cones; list each touched cone with id, link and 'rule to be checked' in the governing by-law or plan and the Public Views Guidelines; quote the dataset caveat, print modified and retrieval dates, label output 'information only, not clearance' and re-check count and ids at every export. 4) Show City names only until review_state release. 5) v1: viewpoints (public or private), 1-degree ray casting for context-only and context-plus-proposal models, and park silhouettes from user-entered coordinates and eye height (1.6 m team preset). Brief-derived values read 'from supplied summary' until confirmed.
visualization: Plan view (v1): wedge per viewpoint, baseline arc grey, proposal teal, lost arc hatched orange, site-plan north arrow used; public solid, private dashed
Elevation silhouette (v1): baseline versus proposal with an angular scale bar in degrees
Table of touched cones with ids, links, dataset caveat, dates and a rule-checked tick box; legend says zero rows is not clearance and output is information only
Georeference stamp on every output; no radar chart, no single score
modules.human_judgment: Which views matter and to whom, what the mountains and water mean to the Nations (the tool does not infer it), whether a loss is acceptable, which by-law governs a touched cone, and whether a material is local in a meaningful sense.
modules.limits: Layer 0 has no terrain by default, so ridge lines need a DEM. Cone data has no heights; the governing by-law was not identified and the guidelines are unopened. Entrants probably cannot get authoritative cone heights before 30 Nov (views@ is closed to them), so cone output is information only. Brief coordinates unavailable and kept local. No cultural-significance data is computed.

modules.name: Ethical AI, authorship and anonymity-safe provenance ledger with offline PDF strip and competition-project mode
modules.design_question: Can every result, image and sentence show who or what made it, what each person decided, and from which sources, while a competition entry stays private and a competition export, including PDFs made outside the platform, carries no identifying information?
modules.effort: 10.5 person-days (team assumption, r3: 9). Cut order: 1 offline identity strip, scan and fixture test 4; 2 AI label and IPTC term 2; 3 source-id lint 1.5; 4 glyph check 1; 5 PROV human_contribution and decided_by 2. Private-mode work belongs to the platform packet.
depends_on: All module outputs (as provenance sources; PROV fields only)
Platform project-sharing, fork, gallery and search settings (platform packet): needed for the VTC flag only, not for the offline strip tool
Dated record of all nine private-mode test cases (M08)
Brief anonymity record (person-made, M08); until it exists the strip tool applies generic rules only
PRES export nodes (other packet): optional, not needed by the offline strip tool
inputs: Every node output (metrics, images, text)
Asset manifest (owned here; read by M05)
Contributor handles (pseudonymous, platform mode only)
AI-tool log: model, version, generative yes/no, media kind, prompt hash, date, tool terms link
Per-element human_contribution and decided_by entries
Module licences and source ids
Registry strings and export fonts (from M05)
Final PDF, JPG or PNG files exported outside the platform (InDesign, Illustrator, Rhino), processed locally
Private deny-list (author names, emails, handles, machine user names) in local config, never exported
outputs: provenance.jsonld (entities, activities, agents, human_contribution, decided_by; private)
ai_label_manifest per image (declared level, media kind, IPTC term and URI)
board_appendix.md (AI use, sources, module names and licences only)
strip_checklist (identity fields plus any brief rule recorded by a person)
strip_scan_report (per file: deny-list hits, startxref count, /Prev, image metadata, XMP history)
export_checklist (shows contribution and decision records; not printed on boards)
vtc_flag_state (available, or blocked with local-mode notice)

parameters.name: offline_strip_tool
parameters.unit: local command-line tool (pikepdf over qpdf; ExifTool for non-PDF images); no upload; accepts any PDF, JPG or PNG; first entrant deliverable
parameters.relationship: Entrants lay out boards in InDesign or Illustrator and render elsewhere, so the platform's export never sees the submitted file. A local tool run on the final files closes that gap and depends on neither PRES export nor the hosted platform.

parameters.name: pdf_strip_pipeline
parameters.unit: ordered steps: 1 delete /Info and catalog XMP; 2 delete page, object and image-level XMP and history; 3 strip image metadata; 4 write a minimal XMP holding only the IPTC term; 5 full qpdf rewrite; 6 scan
parameters.relationship: ExifTool PDF edits are reversible incremental updates that never delete old data, so author fields stay recoverable. Deleting current values first, then fully rewriting, leaves nothing to recover. A file that skips the rewrite fails the gate.

parameters.name: pdf_scan_rules
parameters.unit: raw bytes plus a qpdf --qdf decompressed copy; private deny-list; patterns for user paths, emails, GPS and xmpMM history; startxref and /Prev counts
parameters.relationship: A scan of current tags reports 0 while old revisions and compressed objects keep names. Non-linearized output must show one startxref and no /Prev (a linearized file legitimately shows two). Any hit fails; unknown private-data entries go to a person.

parameters.name: image_and_backup_rules
parameters.unit: per embedded image stream and per standalone file; output to a new folder; fail if any *_original file remains
parameters.relationship: Embedded images keep their own EXIF, XMP and GPS, and ExifTool keeps *_original backups by default. The tool strips every image, never edits in place, and refuses to finish while a backup or untouched copy sits in the export folder.

parameters.name: vtc_flag_release_rule
parameters.unit: fixed rule: the VTC entry flag is selectable only when M08 holds a dated, passing record of all nine private-mode test cases; otherwise a fixed notice shows
parameters.relationship: Without verified private, no-fork, no-index projects, a flagged entry would sit in default public, forkable mode with handles, risking cl. 4.1, 5.1 and 5.3. The notice says: do not create the competition project on the hosted platform; work locally and run the offline strip tool.

parameters.name: competition_project_mode
parameters.unit: on by default when the VTC entry flag is set: private, no forks, no gallery or search listing, noindex, handles hidden until a person records that results are published
parameters.relationship: A project, fork graph or gallery image visible before results can link an entry to its authors (cl. 5.1, 5.3) and count as previous publication (cl. 4.1). Unhiding is a person's action keyed to the verified results date (r3 used 26 Jan 2027 from an unverified summary; S66 says January 2027).

parameters.name: public_sharing_block
parameters.unit: warn-and-block on any public share of a board image before results
parameters.relationship: A public post of a board image can break cl. 4.1 and de-anonymise the team. Blocking and warning keeps entry images unpublished until results; the organizer judges any violation.

parameters.name: brief_anonymity_rules
parameters.unit: person-recorded paraphrase of the brief's anonymity clause and any file or board naming rule, with brief version and date
parameters.relationship: The brief may add rules the Terms lack (file names, board codes). Each recorded rule is added to the strip checklist before export mode is released; without the record, the tool runs generic rules only and says so.

parameters.name: ai_involvement
parameters.unit: enum: none; assistive non-generative; assistive generative edit; composite with AI elements; generated; plus media_kind: capture, authored drawing or render, montage
parameters.relationship: The declared level sets the visible label and IPTC term (see mapping). Splitting generative from non-generative edits stops generative fill being labelled as enhancement. Under-declaring breaks trust.

parameters.name: iptc_term_mapping
parameters.unit: capture unedited: digitalCapture; capture edited, no AI: humanEdits; authored drawing or render, no AI: digitalCreation; montage of renders and captures, no AI: composite; all-capture montage: compositeCapture; non-generative AI assist: algorithmicallyEnhanced; generative edit: compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia; composite with AI elements: compositeSynthetic; generated: trainedAlgorithmicMedia
parameters.relationship: Each label shows the IPTC definition and URI. When unsure, use the term that discloses more AI use. 'Composite' says any element may or may not be generative, so the visible label states the declared level. Vocabulary re-read each release; terms retire. Team mapping.

parameters.name: human_contribution
parameters.unit: enum per element: concept, selection, edit, none
parameters.relationship: Records what a person contributed to each element. AI authorship law is unsettled and the Terms require original work, so the record shows the team's actual role. Shown in the export checklist, not on boards.

parameters.name: decided_by
parameters.unit: enum per decision: code, AI, person
parameters.relationship: Course rule: separate what code, AI and people decide. Stored in the PROV record so the export checklist shows who decided each element and nothing is credited to a person who did not decide it.

parameters.name: authorship_status_rule
parameters.unit: fixed rule: the tool never states copyright or ownership status
parameters.relationship: CIPO registered an AI co-author (SURYAST); CIPPIC's July 2024 application to expunge is pending; ISED consulted on AI and copyright. Terms cl. 12.3 keep authorship with the participant. The tool records contributions only.

parameters.name: contributor_identity_mode
parameters.unit: enum platform mode (handles and fork authors kept) or competition-export mode (all removed)
parameters.relationship: Handles give attribution on the platform. For export every handle, fork author and author field is removed from boards, appendix and file metadata by the strip pipeline, because the Terms bar marks identifying the author's source.

parameters.name: content_credentials_mode
parameters.unit: enum off (default, forced off in competition mode), platform-signed, user-signed
parameters.relationship: A C2PA manifest carries the signer certificate chain and a claim-generator name, so a SALA-identifiable signer could signal origin. If on outside competition mode, use a neutral organisation name and generic claim-generator text, both listed in the metadata panel.

parameters.name: tool_content_badge
parameters.unit: badge on every tool-authored card or list: AI-drafted, human-checked (who and when, platform-side)
parameters.relationship: The platform's own card paraphrases, crosswalk summaries and phrase lists are drafted by AI research agents through a summarising fetch tool. The badge tells users which content a person has checked.

parameters.name: human_review_of_ai_text
parameters.unit: named reviewer (platform record), date; board AI-text label rule
parameters.relationship: AI-drafted board text is declared in the appendix with its extent (drafted or edited); AI-drafted cultural text needs a named reviewer. EU Art. 50(4) review exception and the Canadian code's human oversight are benchmarks. Reviewer's name stays off export.

parameters.name: source_citation_completeness
parameters.unit: share of results with source ids
parameters.relationship: A result without a source id cannot be checked, so it shows as unsourced and its thresholds turn into editable team assumptions.

parameters.name: module_licence_and_attribution_chain
parameters.unit: SPDX id and upstream links
parameters.relationship: A forked module inherits upstream attribution; an incompatible licence raises a merge warning. The appendix lists module names and licences only, not authors. SPDX list not opened.

parameters.name: image_licence_record
parameters.unit: per image: licence or AI-tool terms link, date
parameters.relationship: The Terms require originality and non-infringement and let the organizer ask for image licences; Buildner tells entrants to check AI tools' terms. A per-image record lets the team answer quickly.

parameters.name: export_glyph_coverage
parameters.unit: codepoints with a glyph in the embedded fonts
parameters.relationship: Nation-language strings use combining marks. If an embedded font lacks a glyph, the PDF shows a box or a substitute, which misrepresents the name on the board.

metrics.name: VTC flag selectable without a dated, passing record of all nine private-mode test cases
metrics.basis: Platform rule backed by Terms cl. 4.1, 5.1, 5.3. Whether a private page counts as published is the organizer's call; the tool must not invite public mode.
metrics.method: Check flag availability against the M08 record and its date.

metrics.name: Brief opened with version, date and anonymity clause recorded before export mode is released
metrics.good: yes
metrics.basis: Strip rules rest on an unread brief (S35, four rounds); any extra brief rule must reach the strip checklist.
metrics.method: Check the record in M08.

metrics.name: Entry assets publicly reachable before results (project page, fork graph, gallery, search, shared board images)
metrics.good: 0 until a person records that results are published
metrics.basis: Platform rule backed by Terms cl. 4.1 (no previously published visual materials), 5.1 and 5.3 (anonymity until winners are chosen). Whether a private page counts as published is the organizer's call.
metrics.method: Run the nine M08 cases; a person checks social posts.

metrics.name: Results or claims without a source id
metrics.basis: Course rule: every result cites its source.
metrics.method: Scan provenance graph.

metrics.name: Elements without human_contribution and decided_by records
metrics.basis: Course rule: separate what code, AI and people decide; AI authorship law is unsettled.
metrics.method: Scan PROV records for the two fields.

metrics.name: AI-involved images without both a visible label and an embedded digital source type
metrics.basis: IPTC gives the terms; the Canadian code expects transparency; EU Art. 50(2) is a benchmark only and reportedly applies from 2 Dec 2026, not 2 Aug 2026.
metrics.method: Check metadata and overlay per image.

metrics.name: Images whose IPTC term does not match the declared level and media kind (AI understated, or a capture labelled digitalCreation)
metrics.basis: r2 mapped composite and assistive edit to the wrong terms; r3 mapped every non-AI image to digitalCreation, which IPTC defines as human creation with non-generative tools, not capture (S38).
metrics.method: Compare declared level and media kind with the mapping table and the tool log's generative flag.

metrics.name: Identity-bearing fields in competition export (author, creator, handle, fork author, signer certificate or organisation, GPS, claim-generator string, XMP history paths, any brief-named field), in current values or any earlier revision
metrics.basis: Round 0 marked this verified; the brief was not opened. r4: ExifTool PDF edits are reversible and keep old data (S72, S73), so a current-tag scan could report 0 while names stay recoverable. Embedded images and XMP history are further paths.
metrics.method: Run the pipeline; scan raw bytes and a decompressed copy of the final file for deny-list names, user paths, emails, GPS and history fields; a person reads the brief's anonymity clause.

metrics.name: Strip fixture test passes: PDF with known author, creator, XMP history path and a geotagged embedded JPEG, stripped, then a recovery attempt (exiftool -PDF-update:all=) and a raw scan
metrics.good: yes: 0 hits, one startxref, no /Prev, no GPS in images
metrics.bad: no, or not run, or run before the last tool change
metrics.basis: The pipeline is documented design from S72 to S75, not run. The fixture proves the recovery path is closed. Gate condition for offering the tool.
metrics.method: Run the fixture on Windows and macOS; save the report in M08.

metrics.name: Final PDFs with recoverable earlier metadata (more than one startxref in non-linearized output, /Prev present, or a deny-list hit in raw or decompressed bytes)
metrics.basis: qpdf's default write drops orphaned objects (S74) and the ExifTool page names a qpdf rewrite as the permanent removal (S72); the xref-count test is the team's reading of PDF structure.
metrics.method: Count startxref and /Prev in raw bytes; grep the qpdf --qdf copy.

metrics.name: Tool-authored cards or lists without a provenance badge
metrics.basis: Course rule: show who drafted and who checked; platform content is AI-drafted.
metrics.method: Scan card and list manifests.

metrics.name: Team assumptions shown without the editable-assumption flag
metrics.basis: Platform rule: unsourced thresholds are visible as editable team assumptions.
metrics.method: Compare thresholds with source ids.

metrics.name: AI-drafted cultural text without a named human reviewer
metrics.basis: Human oversight expectation; editorial-review exception in the EU text, as a benchmark.
metrics.method: Check review field.

metrics.name: Images with an AI-tool or licence record missing
metrics.basis: Terms let the organizer request image licences and put infringement liability on the participant.
metrics.method: Check register.

metrics.name: Registry codepoints without a glyph in the embedded export fonts
metrics.basis: Font coverage is untested; a person also checks mark placement.
metrics.method: Map codepoints to glyphs per embedded font (fontTools).

modules.method: Each node run writes a W3C PROV-style JSON-LD record: output, node, handle or tool, inputs, source ids, human_contribution, decided_by. The VTC flag appears only when M08 holds a dated pass for all nine private-mode cases; otherwise a notice says to work locally and use the offline strip tool. Export, on the platform or offline: (a) PDFs: pikepdf deletes /Info, XMP and object or image metadata, qpdf rewrites the whole file, ExifTool never writes PDFs; (b) images are stripped into a new folder; (c) raw bytes and a decompressed copy are scanned for deny-list names, user paths, GPS and history fields; (d) the mapped IPTC term and a visible AI label are embedded; (e) Content Credentials stay off; (f) an appendix lists AI use, sources, module names and licences; (g) glyphs and source ids are linted. Prompts are hashed in the browser. The gate fails if any rule fails.
visualization: Lineage graph: output to activity to agent, coloured human, AI-assisted or AI-generated (platform view only)
Corner provenance badge on every result card: author type, source count, AI-drafted human-checked state
VTC flag panel: available with test date, or blocked with the local-mode notice
Strip report: per-file table of deny-list hits, startxref count, image metadata, fixture-test date; fix link per failure
Export checklist with pass/fail rows, contribution and decision records; false assumptions kept visible
Before-and-after metadata panel: identity fields removed per file, plus any neutral signer or claim-generator text
modules.human_judgment: Whether AI use is appropriate for each element, what each person contributed, accountability for every statement, authorship claims, choosing the deny-list, opening a stripped PDF to check it, reading the competition rules and brief, running the private-mode test, and the decision to publish after results.
modules.limits: Strip pipeline is documented design from S72 to S75, not yet run; fixture test gates it. InDesign, Illustrator and browser exports may embed private data or image metadata the scan must be tuned on (unverified). Labels are declared and lost when platforms strip metadata; C2PA does not prove authorship. Brief anonymity clause unread. Private page versus published is the organizer's call. EU dates and Canadian AI copyright unsettled.

modules.name: Cultural-context readiness register, content-keyed review gate and board-statement builder
modules.design_question: Which cultural-context claims can the boards honestly make today, what evidence and Indigenous-review status back each, and what do entrants actually get before 30 Nov 2026?
modules.effort: 5 person-days (the review_state flag in module manifests ships earlier, in core)
inputs: Outputs and gates of M01-M07
Board outline from PRES
Jury criterion text for cultural context (supplied summary until brief confirmed)
Review records (reviewer, scope, date, consent to be named)
Ethics-check record (instructor, BREB answer)
Private-mode test results per case (platform packet, dated)
Source snapshot, brief and Terms IP-clause records (person-made)
Buildner access log (date, channel, result)
Author declarations, Buildner associate reply, instructor confirmation (records only)
Strip fixture test record (M07)
outputs: review_state_register.json (per module, list, card deck and Nation string)
entrant_scope.json (what ships to entrants before 30 Nov, with dates, and the fallback scope)
release_preconditions.json (private-mode cases, Terms snapshot, brief record, Terms IP clause, eligibility records, fixture test)
export_gate_M08 (M01, M05 where released, M07 must pass)

parameters.name: claim
parameters.unit: text with evidence type
parameters.relationship: A claim needs matching evidence (geometry from M06, source from M02 or M04, provenance from M05, status from M01); a claim without it is demoted to intent wording.

parameters.name: criterion_item
parameters.unit: enum City in Nature, cultural-geographic-environmental character, reconciliation and Indigenous perspectives
parameters.relationship: Each criterion item gets a coverage state, not a score: coverage is not quality, and the jury judges quality. Wording shows 'from supplied summary' until the brief is confirmed.

parameters.name: needs_nation_input
parameters.unit: list
parameters.relationship: Items only a Nation can answer stay open and visible, so the boards do not fill the gap with the team's own voice.

parameters.name: review_state
parameters.unit: enum unreviewed prototype, reviewed (scope, reviewer, date), released; keyed to content
parameters.relationship: Any module, list or card that renders a Nation-language string, a cultural prompt card or a cultural phrase list is gated, whatever its category. Unreviewed items are hidden from entrants. Exemption rule: stage A ships only claim-restricting rules and fixed text with no cultural content, frozen by hash; any addition is gated.

parameters.name: entrant_scope_for_vtc_2026
parameters.unit: fixed statement plus a dated panel: available now / not before 30 Nov, generated from entrant_scope.json; fallback text if the brief is not obtained
parameters.relationship: Entrants get the offline strip tool, M01 stage A, M06 geometry (City names only) and M07 in cut order; CULT cards, lists and Nation strings follow review, likely after 30 Nov. The panel stops entrants assuming the tool covers the 30% criterion or arrives whole.

parameters.name: buildner_contingency
parameters.unit: decision date 27 Oct 2026 (team assumption); access log of date, channel, result; pre-written fallback scope
parameters.relationship: Buildner pages failed in four rounds and registration closes 29 Oct. By 27 Oct a person checks Buildner status through its general support channel (never a juror or advisor). If the brief is not obtained: M07 export mode and the full contact guard do not ship; entrants get M01 stage A, M06 geometry and the offline strip tool on generic rules.

parameters.name: core_cut_order
parameters.unit: ordered list with team target dates: 1 offline strip, scan and fixture test, 2 AI label and IPTC term (by 13 Nov); 3 source-id lint, 4 glyph check (by 20 Nov); 5 PROV fields if time; ray casting v1
parameters.relationship: If time runs short, later steps drop first, so entrants never rely on a feature that has not shipped. A dropped step moves to 'not before 30 Nov' in the panel. The strip tool is not offered without a passing fixture test. Dates are team assumptions.

parameters.name: private_mode_test_cases
parameters.unit: nine cases, each with tester, date, request, response evidence, pass or fail: 1 logged-out project URL; 2 direct asset, CDN or storage URLs and signed-link expiry; 3 social-preview (OG) tags and thumbnails; 4 sitemap, robots, noindex header and meta tag; 5 fork, clone and export API; 6 gallery and search listings; 7 activity feeds, profiles and history showing handles; 8 cached thumbnails after a visibility change; 9 any linked public repository. Record valid 14 days or until a deploy touches sharing, auth or assets (team assumption)
parameters.relationship: A shallow test could pass while assets stay public. Any case that returns entry content without login fails, however hard the URL is to guess. robots.txt Disallow alone does not keep a URL out of search, so case 4 checks noindex. One fail keeps the VTC flag blocked.

parameters.name: release_preconditions
parameters.unit: records: dated nine-case private-mode record; verified Terms and jury snapshot (M01); brief version, date and anonymity clause (M07); Terms IP and confidentiality clause reference; author declarations, Buildner associate reply and instructor confirmation (M01); strip fixture test
parameters.relationship: M07 export mode and the VTC flag do not ship until the matching record exists; the contact guard shows only its generic rule until the snapshot is verified. Unmet preconditions show on the entrant panel.

parameters.name: reviewer_independence
parameters.unit: declared: not a Nation referral office, not tied to any juror, not a Buildner advisor or in-house juror for VTC 2026, consent to be named
parameters.relationship: A referral office would use the staff time M01 asks entrants to spare; a reviewer tied to a juror or to Buildner's cultural advisors (cl. 10.4) could breach contact rules or conflict. Declared in the record. Team rule.

parameters.name: reviewer_plan
parameters.unit: budget line (amount and source named by the team), contact deadline 28 Oct 2026, written fallback
parameters.relationship: No reviewer, budget or contact exists and registration closes in 8 days. Fallback if no signed-off reviewer by 13 Nov: no CULT content ships for VTC 2026. The deadline is a team assumption.

parameters.name: ethics_check
parameters.unit: record: instructor and UBC BREB answer, date
parameters.relationship: User tests with student teams and Indigenous review may be research with participants. TCPS 2 Art. 2.1 covers course-based activities; Art. 2.5 exempts only assessment testing; Ch. 9 applies if Indigenous people take part; UBC's Indigenous review page adds questions. modules.method: The node collects state from M01-M07 and builds a three-column register: claim, evidence and source, status (evidenced, intent only, needs Nation input, out of scope). It lists the review_state of every module, list, deck and Nation string, keyed to content; anything unreviewed is hidden from entrants, and course demos carry a prototype ribbon. It records the entrant scope with dates and the fallback scope, the core cut order, release preconditions (nine private-mode cases, Terms snapshot, brief record, IP clause, eligibility records, fixture test), the reviewer plan, the ethics check and the Buildner access log. It generates board text skeletons: per-Nation engagement statement (M01), AI-use-and-sources appendix (M07), cultural-material provenance note (M05) and a limits statement. The user rewrites all narrative. The export gate refuses to pass if M01 or M07 fail, or M05 where released. No metric becomes a cultural-quality number.

case_studies.tool: Local Contexts (TK Labels, BC Labels, Notices, Hub)
case_studies.what_it_does: Lets Indigenous communities attach conditions to cultural material (Labels) and lets institutions flag Indigenous interests (Notices: Engagement, Disclosure, Collections Care).
case_studies.workflow_step: Provenance and permission of any Indigenous-derived asset (M05)

case_studies.stops_at: Cannot decide whether a use is permitted; the tool cannot assign Labels for a community.
case_studies.license_cost: Icons and template text copyrighted by Local Contexts; Hub terms and API guide not reviewed.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Prompt when an asset is tagged cultural but has no Hub record.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Deciding who holds authority over knowledge or whether permission is real.

case_studies.what_it_does: Open-source platform where communities set cultural protocols as access levels, with TK Labels built in.

case_studies.what_it_does: Nation-run interactive map with Elder audio in hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓, photos and a children's book.

case_studies.tool: C2PA Content Credentials with IPTC Digital Source Type
case_studies.what_it_does: Open standard for signed provenance records, plus a vocabulary for marking images as captured, human-made, AI-edited or AI-generated.
case_studies.workflow_step: Labelling AI output on boards and exports (M07)
case_studies.how_used: Embed the mapped IPTC term (capture: digitalCapture; no-AI render: digitalCreation; generative edit: compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia; composite with AI elements: compositeSynthetic; generated: trainedAlgorithmicMedia) and a visible label. Credentials off in competition mode; if on, neutral organisation and generic claim-generator text.
case_studies.strengths: Open specification (2.3); open-source SDK; identity optional; IPTC terms have stable URIs and published definitions.
case_studies.stops_at: Labels are declared and easily stripped; they do not prove authorship or permission; a certificate chain and claim-generator name travel with every manifest; IPTC retires terms.
case_studies.license_cost: c2pa-rs MIT OR Apache-2.0; spec 2.3 licence not confirmed; certificates may cost money (unverified).
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Auto-fill labels from the tool's own generation log, including its generative yes/no flag and media kind.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Whether using AI for a given element is appropriate.

case_studies.tool: ExifTool with qpdf and pikepdf (PDF and image metadata removal)
case_studies.what_it_does: ExifTool reads and writes metadata in many formats; qpdf rewrites PDF files; pikepdf scripts qpdf from Python and edits /Info and XMP.
case_studies.workflow_step: Anonymity strip and scan of final boards (M07)
case_studies.how_used: pikepdf deletes current /Info and XMP and object metadata, qpdf rewrites the whole file, ExifTool strips non-PDF images and only reads PDFs; a raw-byte scan and a fixture test check the result.
case_studies.strengths: Open source; qpdf Apache-2.0 and pikepdf MPL-2.0 per their READMEs; documentation states the rewrite step that removes old data.
case_studies.stops_at: ExifTool PDF edits are reversible incremental updates and keep old data; none of the tools proves a file has no identifying content, and private application data is untested.
case_studies.license_cost: qpdf Apache-2.0; pikepdf MPL-2.0; ExifTool Perl Artistic or GPL (not verified).
case_studies.ai_opportunity: None for the strip itself; AI could suggest deny-list candidates from the project README for a person to confirm.
